about.title: Cudahy Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Medical malpractice cases carry a different set of rules than a typical injury claim, and that matters if something went wrong during your care in or near Cudahy. California's MICRA framework requires a 90-day notice before a lawsuit is filed, sets tight windows for bringing a claim, and almost always calls for a qualified medical expert to weigh in on what happened. A bad result from surgery or a missed diagnosis is not automatically malpractice — the law asks whether the care fell below an accepted medical standard. For residents in this densely populated pocket of Los Angeles County, getting a knowledgeable read on your situation early can matter, since the notice and filing deadlines move faster than people expect. LawProactive doesn't practice law itself; we simply connect you, at no cost, with an independent attorney experienced in evaluating these claims so you can understand your options.

items.title: Deadlines Move Fast
items.desc: California generally gives one year from when you discover the harm, capped at three years from the injury, and a 90-day pre-suit notice must go out before a lawsuit can even be filed. Missing these steps can end a claim before it starts.

items.title: Expert Review Is Almost Always Required
items.desc: Because a bad outcome alone doesn't prove malpractice, a qualified medical expert typically has to confirm the care fell below an accepted standard. An attorney familiar with this process can help line up that kind of review.

items.title: Non-Economic Damages Are Capped, But the Cap Rises
items.desc: California law places a statutory limit on non-economic damages in these cases, and that cap increases each year. Understanding where the current cap stands is one reason to get an informed opinion on your specific situation.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a medical malpractice claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, you have one year from when you discover (or reasonably should have discovered) the injury, but no more than three years from the date it happened. A 90-day notice to the healthcare provider is also required before filing suit. These timelines can be tricky, so it's worth having someone review your specific dates.

items.question: Is every bad medical outcome considered malpractice?
items.answer: No. California law requires showing that the care you received fell below the accepted standard for that type of treatment, not just that the result was disappointing or painful. That's why a qualified medical expert is almost always brought in to evaluate the case.

items.question: I live in Cudahy — does it matter where my treatment happened?
items.answer: What matters most is where the care was provided and which healthcare facility or provider was involved, not simply your home address. If your treatment occurred at a clinic or hospital serving the Cudahy area, an independent attorney can look into the details of that specific provider and the care you received.
